programme.question: Missing Data Art, read through human extinction
Missing Data Art, read through human extinction by AI

findings.line: The evidence on AI and extinction is produced by the parties it concerns; the missing datum that could exist is an observer who fixed the recording rule before looking.
every stand-in for the record an extinction cannot leave is kept by someone who must outlive it; ask of any evidence who would be left to write its other answer.
When an outcome can never be observed, each stand-in for it (who answered, what can be paid out, what is scored) rewards something other than being right about the world.

programme.question: What does the world record of the catastrophes that almost happened, and who decides that a near miss counts?

findings.line: Who decides a near miss depends on the record's rule: a reader under a definition, a keeper under a list, a telescope under a formula; a next question can ask which rule a record of AI dangers should have.
A near miss is half a sentence until someone joins a hinge to a catastrophe; few records write both, so a next question can ask who should write the other half, and when.
A near miss can wait as long for the record when nobody knew as when somebody did; a next question can ask who holds a near miss before it is public, and what that custody does to the count.

programme.question: What does the world record of a danger before it arrives, and who keeps the warnings: the ones heeded, the ones ignored and the ones never needed?

findings.line: Warning records score hits, half-score false alarms and cannot see prevention; prevention became visible only where a keeper published, in advance, a second column for what would happen without acting.

Of a warning's three fates the world writes only "ignored", "never needed" only where nobody acted or acting changes nothing, and "heeded" only the warner, as its own counterfactual; a next question can ask who could audit it.

Asked to back a visitor's filings of real warnings, the record contradicted "never needed" for one in six and confirmed no fate at all; a next question can ask what a record must keep for a fate to be checkable.

programme.question: When a warning turns out never needed, who pays for it, and does a record of false alarms make the next warning less believed?

findings.line: Casualties cannot tell a public that learns from false alarms from one that stops listening; the cry-wolf effect has to be measured in people, and only who pays for an obeyed empty warning is measurable from records.

A record of false alarms rightly lowers belief for a reader who learns, briefly and repaid at the next hit; only a reader who counts runs charges the liar's price, and nobody writes down the price of taking cover.
Some missing data is kept by the people it is missing from: a record of stars not seen measured the night's loss where satellites missed it; next, who else keeps such negative records?

An absence already filled keeps its mood only while its mark lasts; a training corpus keeps the marks its task needs and turns the rest of the editor's writing into evidence, so ask which marks it sorted out.
